chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Satan tempts (causes discord) among the believers as long as one of them does not return from his religion. So when they do that, he lies down on his back and stretches, then says, 'I have succeeded.' May Allah have mercy on the man who unites two of our friends. O group of believers! Be united and sympathetic (to each other).

key_terms.يُغْرِي: tempts or causes to be deceived/estranged

ai.seo_question: How does Satan tempt believers and what is the remedy according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) illustrates Satan's posture of defeat when believers maintain unity, emphasizing that his influence wanes as long as they do not abandon their faith. The Imam’s exhortation to 'reconcile and show affection' (ta'alluf wa ta'ataffuf) highlights the Shia emphasis on social cohesion (tawarrud) as a spiritual defense mechanism against external and internal corruption. This narrative underscores the practical application of unity as a direct counter to the devil's strategy of fragmentation within the community.
